subject: FinBridge — post-call eval recap & proposed trial + parity gates
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinBridge — post-call eval recap & proposed trial + parity gates

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and my recommended next steps so we can get a trial started this week if you're ready.

TL;DR: we recommend a 2-week controlled trial (sandbox data) comparing two open-model variants vs your current proprietary baseline. Acceptance = parity on task-level accuracy and no meaningful regression on hallucination or latency.

Key items from the call:
- Primary use case: customer support triage + short-form answer generation (~100–250 tokens).
- Priority metrics: intent classification accuracy (macro F1), answer correctness (human-rated A/B), hallucination rate (QA tests), average token latency (p95).
- Data available: 3k anonymized chat transcripts and 500 human-annotated verification cases.

Our proposed trial plan (high level):
1) Models to trial (we'll run all three in parallel):
   - Open-A: Mixtral-8x7B (8-bit quant) — recommended for quality/cost balance
   - Open-B: Llama-3-13B (Q4_K_M) — higher quality headroom on complex prompts
   - Baseline: your current proprietary model (we'll proxy with your sample outputs for evaluation)

2) Acceptance / parity gates (preliminary, we can tighten after sample evaluation):
   - Intent F1 >= baseline - 2 points (i.e., within 2 percentage points)
   - Human-rated correctness: open model mean score within 0.1 points (on 0–5 scale) of baseline
   - Hallucination rate: absolute increase <= 3% vs baseline on the 500 verification cases
   - Latency (p95): within 1.2x of baseline for 95% of calls; if not, we propose autoscaling plus routing to baseline for latency-critical traffic

3) Evaluation artifacts we will deliver:
   - Benchmark CSV with per-case model outputs + automated metrics (attached snapshot)
   - Prompt bundle (prompt engineering pack + safety transformations) — attached zip
   - Human eval rubric and sample labeling instructions (Drive link below)

4) Operational / rollout notes:
   - We’ll enable per-request model routing so you can pilot open models for a % of traffic and fall back to baseline automatically if regression detected.
   - We recommend enabling prefix KV caching for repeated conversations to reduce cost/latency during the trial.

Next steps / asks from FinBridge:
- Confirm go/no-go for a 2-week sandbox trial (we can start as early as Tue 3/2).
- Provide the anonymized dataset drop link or S3 credentials (read-only) for evaluation.
- Let us know any additional acceptance thresholds you care about (especially for compliance or regulatory checks).

Attachments: finbridge_proposal_promptsets.zip (prompt bundles, eval harness), finbridge-benchmark-snapshot.csv (small sample).
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b-FinBridge-Eval-Pack

I’ll open a trial ticket and assign engineering for a Monday kickoff if you confirm. Happy to jump on a short call to lock scope.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Emily — quick technical notes and an initial ops proposal so procurement has something to pair with the SOW: 

Cost estimate (sandbox, small footprint, 2 weeks): 
- Baseline proxy + 2 open models on 1–2 GPUs each: ~$6,800–$9,500 total (depends on concurrency). We’ll provide a precise quote after we confirm expected concurrency and data ingress method.

Traffic/Isolation: 
- We can run the trial in a dedicated sandbox VPC project and restrict routing to only test accounts / API keys. No production traffic will be affected unless you explicitly enable split routing.

Performance/Config notes: 
- Mixtral-8x7B: use Q4_K_M or 8-bit dynamic; best balance for cost with our runtime kernels. Expect slightly higher token-efficiency vs Llama-3 at some prompt types.
- Llama-3-13B: best for multi-step reasoning; use Q4_K for faster logits but higher memory.
- We recommend enabling continuous KV caching for the triage flows; we’ll also instrument token-level cost/latency tracing so we can correlate regressions to specific prompt patterns.

Canary / rollback policy (ops):
- Start with 5% of test traffic to each open model for 48 hours; run automated checks against the 500 verification cases hourly. If any gate breaches, auto-failover to baseline and notify the trial channel.

I’ll draft an SOW line-item set (trial dates, deliverables, cost breakdown, acceptance criteria) and share it in the next hour. If Emily confirms cost band, Marissa and I will send the SOW to procurement.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
